concepts.name: Cost-aware EBS selection
concepts.description: gp3 decouples baseline storage size from provisioned IOPS and throughput, while io2 targets demanding IOPS and st1 or sc1 target lower-cost sequential throughput workloads.

concepts.name: Cost-aware storage migration and managed transfer
concepts.description: DataSync handles managed online storage transfer, Transfer Family handles managed file-transfer protocols, Storage Gateway supports ongoing hybrid access, and Snow Family is now mainly an exam-recognition/current-customer topic because new customers cannot order Snow devices.

concepts.name: On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, and Spot
concepts.description: On-Demand provides no-commitment flexibility; Savings Plans and RIs reduce eligible committed-usage pricing with different flexibility; Spot provides interruptible spare capacity for fault-tolerant workloads.

concepts.name: Right-sizing, Auto Scaling, and Compute Optimizer
concepts.description: Right-sizing matches resource capacity to measured demand, Auto Scaling adjusts capacity over time, and AWS Compute Optimizer provides recommendations based on utilization data.

concepts.name: Lambda, Fargate, and EC2 cost trade-offs
concepts.description: Lambda charges for requests and execution resources, Fargate charges for provisioned task resources, and EC2 charges for instance capacity with purchasing-model options.

concepts.name: RDS, Aurora Serverless v2, and DynamoDB cost models
concepts.description: Right-size provisioned relational databases, use Aurora Serverless v2 for variable relational ACU demand, and choose DynamoDB on-demand or provisioned capacity from request predictability.

concepts.name: Caching to reduce database cost
concepts.description: A cache can absorb repeated reads and reduce database CPU, I/O, and capacity requirements when the workload has cacheable access patterns.

concepts.name: Database backups and retention cost
concepts.description: Backup frequency and retention determine recovery coverage and storage consumption, so retention should match business and compliance requirements.

concepts.name: NAT gateway and VPC endpoint cost trade-offs
concepts.description: NAT gateways incur hourly and data-processing charges, while VPC endpoints can keep supported service traffic private and may reduce NAT data processing for that traffic.

concepts.name: Data transfer and edge caching cost
concepts.description: Architecture choices that keep traffic local or serve cacheable content from edge locations can reduce origin load and some data-transfer paths.

concepts.name: Peering, Transit Gateway, VPN, and Direct Connect cost
concepts.description: VPC peering, Transit Gateway, Site-to-Site VPN, and Direct Connect have different topology, bandwidth, operational, and data-processing cost characteristics.

concepts.name: Cost Explorer, Budgets, Data Exports/CUR, and allocation tags
concepts.description: Cost Explorer analyzes trends, Budgets monitors thresholds/forecasts, CUR 2.0 via Data Exports provides detailed billing data, and cost allocation tags attribute spend.

concepts.name: Storage access, sizing, backup, and archival economics
concepts.description: Optimize storage by matching access pattern, right-sizing provisioned storage, using Requester Pays where appropriate, and aligning backup/archive retention with actual recovery and compliance needs.

concepts.name: Availability, hibernation, and elastic compute cost
concepts.description: Match availability to workload class, stop or scale in idle non-production capacity where acceptable, and use EC2 hibernation when preserving RAM state is valuable.

concepts.name: Database connections, read scaling, and migration cost
concepts.description: Use RDS Proxy for connection pooling, read replicas for read scaling, AWS DMS for data migration, and DMS Schema Conversion when moving between different engines.

concepts.name: Network throttling and bandwidth cost controls
concepts.description: Use rate/burst throttling to control request pressure and size hybrid bandwidth from measured requirements instead of overprovisioning.

questions.prompt: A non-production EC2 application takes a long time to rebuild a large in-memory working set. It is unused overnight, and the team wants to stop paying instance-usage charges while preserving RAM state for the next morning. Which feature should it evaluate?

options.label: Convert the stateful workload blindly to Spot

questions.explanation: EC2 hibernation saves RAM state to the EBS root volume and the instance enters a stopped state. Instance usage is not charged while stopped, although EBS and other persisting resources can still incur charges.
hints: The requirement is to stop compute billing while preserving memory state.

error_codes.description: EC2 hibernation was not selected for resumable stopped state.

questions.prompt: Match each database cost driver to the mechanism that directly addresses it.

slots.label: Bursty clients create too many short-lived DB connections
Read-only traffic drives primary DB capacity
Migration changes database engine and requires schema conversion

questions.explanation: RDS Proxy reduces connection overhead, read replicas offload read traffic, and heterogeneous database migrations can use AWS DMS plus DMS Schema Conversion.
hints: Identify whether the cost driver is connections, read capacity, or migration work.

error_codes.description: A database cost driver was matched incorrectly.

questions.prompt: A public REST API experiences short request bursts that cause expensive downstream scaling. The business wants to enforce a controlled steady request rate and burst target at the API layer. Which mechanism fits?

options.label: API Gateway rate and burst throttling

questions.explanation: API Gateway supports rate and burst throttling targets, which can limit excessive request pressure before it reaches downstream systems.
hints: The control belongs at the API request-rate layer.

error_codes.description: API rate/burst throttling was not selected.
